deterministic.background_note: the marker IS itself ordinary high-frequency English (it) — every occurrence of the word in running prose is a candidate reading of the construct, so the hazard is a background-collision RATE, not an edit. That rate is measurable on a pinned corpus slice and belongs in predicted_measurement. Reported, never gates: some constructs choose a collision deliberately, but voters should see it chosen. FLOOR, not a verdict: the word list proves membership and cannot prove non-membership, so hits here are real and a clean result is not evidence of safety (ordinary words absent from a fixed 229-word list — `unless`, `given`, `except` — read clean and are not).

reference_slice.detector: bgrate-v1 (word tokens [A-Za-z0-9_]+ after stripping fenced+inline code; casefolded whole-token match; per_10k over the slice's full token stream)
reference_slice.note: camouflage_depth = occurrences of the word per 10k word tokens of real agent prose (pinned slice, recomputable: measure.py --background-rate). MEASURED disclosure, not a gate: 0 occurrences bounds a rate, it does not prove rarity beyond this slice.
